evidence_items.locator: Section 4.3 and Tables 1 and 6; quoted sentence in Appendix A
evidence_items.explanation: Using the same LM scoring rule, the largest GPT-2 and GPT-3 models score respectively 69.0% and 85.2% on COPA, 67.6% and 79.3% on StoryCloze, and 38.4% and 57.6% on HellaSwag. These comparisons support broad improvement, but measure selected-answer accuracy rather than the probability of generating a correct answer on each prompt.

evidence_items.explanation: TruthfulQA supplies a material qualification to broad improvement: larger models did not improve on every evaluation. Its reported trend does not by itself establish that GPT-3 generally assigns less probability to correct answers than GPT-2.

The main generation results evaluate a deterministic decoding rule, not repeated random samples. The paper also examines normalized likelihood over reference answers and higher-temperature GPT-3 outputs, but these do not supply the matched GPT-2-versus-GPT-3 sampling comparison required here.

unresolved_gaps: The located evidence does not establish a general increase in correct-answer probability across matched GPT-2 and GPT-3 prompts under comparable sampling settings.
The speaker supplies neither an example distribution nor a decoding protocol. Benchmark accuracy cannot close that gap without an additional interpretation.
